title: Telemetry-weighted alert sieve with graceful region evacuation runbooks
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Goal: Build an alerting ensemble — the Telemetry-Weighted Alert Sieve (TWAS) — that reduces noisy pages while enabling deterministic, automated progressive region evacuation for genuine degradations. TWAS combines multiple signals (SLO burn rate, request latency distribution, error-class fingerprinting, KV cache hit ratios, and routing fallbacks) into a telemetry score to gate paging and trigger orchestrated load-shedding and circuit-breaker escalation sequences. Deliverables: 1) scoring engine and policy config, 2) region-aware circuit-breaker profiles, 3) staged load-shedding policies (graceful -> aggressive), 4) canonical on-call runbooks with automated playflows for mitigation and rollback, 5) dashboard for score calibration and simulation harness, 6) synthetic canaries and test harness for safety. Why: Current paging flood during transient noisy telemetry and noisy tail-latency leads to oncall fatigue and slower mitigations. Approach: prefer scoring + hold windows over hard thresholds; prefer automatic low-risk mitigations (eg. route to backup region, widen latency p95 SLO acceptance bands) before human page; escalate to full pager only when telemetry score crosses high-confidence band or after automatic mitigation fails. Trade-offs considered: - Risk of under-alerting vs. oncall burnout: mitigate by conservative initial thresholds and a soft-fail safe mode that pages if downstream customer-impact metric moves. - Automation safety: every automated mitigation must be reversible and have a visible audit trail. - Complexity vs. operator comprehension: keep runbooks linear with annotated decision points and measurable checkpoints. Key success metrics: 30–50% reduction in P1 pages attributable to noise within 3 months, median time-to-detect reduced by 15% for region-impact incidents, and fewer cross-region escalations. Implementation plan: 1) prototype scoring engine and simulation (2 sprints), 2) integrate with existing alerting router and incidents API (1 sprint), 3) circuit-breaker profiles + autoscaling tie-ins (1 sprint), 4) runbook authoring and automated playflows in runbooks service (1 sprint), 5) rollout with canary on non-prod region (2 weeks), 6) staged production rollout by team/region. Compliance: audit logs and KMS-signed actions for automated mitigation steps for Private deployments. Interop: must work with existing SLO service, Runtime-Health metrics, Console tracing, and the Runbooks automation service. Delivery owner: Reliability team + Runbooks infra.

acceptance_criteria: 1) TWAS scoring engine running in staging and producing per-incident telemetry scores
2) Router integrates score to suppress pages below configured threshold and triggers automated mitigation steps
3) Circuit-breaker profiles can be dynamically adjusted and recorded in CB service
4) On-call runbook authoring includes automated mitigation steps and one-click rollback
5) Dashboard shows historical score vs. pages and expected reduction estimator
6) Canary rollout on non-prod with at least 2 scheduled chaos runs and measured improvement
